newsitem.title: SWEDEN: FOCUS-Nordbanken says buy-back boosts stock price.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Nordbanken says buy-back boosts stock price.

text.p: Sweden's state-controlled Nordbanken on Wednesday posted strong profits for the first nine months of the year and said its recent share buy-back had helped bolster share prices almost 20 percent.

Nordbanken posted a nine-month operating profit of 5.74 billion crowns ($874 million) compared with the same period in 1995, pinning the increase to better transaction revenues, strongly reduced credit losses and lower operating costs.
Earnings per share rose by 1.68 crowns to 18.77, while loan losses fell to 489 million crowns from 966 million in the first nine months of 1995.
Last month's, five billion crown share buy-back had a positive impact on the share price, Nordbanken said.

"The sharemarket has recieved the share buy-back very positively, and the move was behind the positive development of the Nordbanken share compared with the previous quarterly result," Nordbanken said.
In fact, the share price has appreciated to around 167 crowns from its level of 135.50 immediately prior to the buy-back announcement on September 11.

The bank priced the 32 million shares in the buy-back -- which was targeted at the state's holding -- at 155 crowns. Through the buy-back, the government's holding was reduced to 59.4 percent from 65.5 percent.

Net profit from financial transactions jumped to 1.03 billion crowns from 366 million crowns. Staff costs rose to 2.12 billion crowns from 2.06 billion, while other costs fell to 2.46 billion from 2.77 billion crowns.
"A strong net improvement in (income from) financial transactions, sharply reduced loan losses and lower operating costs led to improved results, while the interest net worsened," Nordbanken said.
It said net interest income fell to 20.80 billion crowns in the period from 22.38 billion crowns.

"Depressed margins, especially on deposits, led to a seven percent decrease in the interest net compared with the same 1995 period, despite the fact that lending volumes were 11 percent higher," the bank said.
Net interest income was also hit by costs for the state deposit guarantee which banks have had to bear since the beginning of the year, Nordbanken said.
"The cost for Nordbanken will amount to 200 million crowns on a half-year basis and will be included in interest costs."

Sweden's top commercial bank Handelsbanken on Tuesday posted a 19 percent rise in earnings for the first nine months of the year, saying investment banking and improved interest income were behind the improvement.
Handelsbanken's profit after loan losses increased to 4.52 billion crowns from the 3.79 billion shown in the first nine months of last year. ($1=6.568 Swedish Crown)
